 Minimum Wage Increases to $16.48 Per Hour
 By Frank L. Cahill 
 Oct 18, 2026 
 0 
 617 
 Share 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin ReddIt Email Print Copy URL 
 Advertisement 
 Advertisement 
 TRENTON — The minimum wage for most employees in New Jersey will rise to $16.48 per hour on Friday, January 1, an increase of $0.56 over the current rate. Employers must adjust their payroll to comply with the new rates.
 Additional rates taking effect January 1 include:
 Agricultural workers: $15.00 per hour, up from $14.20
 Seasonal and small employers (fewer than six employees): $16.25 per hour, up from $15.23
 Long-term care direct care staff: $19.48 per hour, up from $18.92
 Tipped workers (minimum cash wage): $6.61 per hour, up from $6.05, with a maximum tip credit of $9.87
 If a tipped worker’s minimum cash wage plus tips does not equal the state minimum wage, the employer must pay the difference.
